scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The DHCP server daemon (isc-dhcp-server / dhcpd) on r1 has crashed and is no longer
running. The process that held PID 87 no longer exists ("No such process"), yet a stale
/var/run/dhcpd.pid file remains on disk; systemctl/service reports the unit as
"inactive (dead)". R1 hosts the single centralised DHCP server for the entire site:
its address 10.0.0.76 is bound to r1's loopback interface, and every distribution
switch relay agent (dswa1's dhcrelay on VLANs 10/20/40/99, dswb1's dhcrelay on VLANs
10/20/30/99) unicasts all DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST packets to that address. With
dhcpd dead there is no listener on UDP/67 at 10.0.0.76, so all relayed DHCP discovery
traffic is silently discarded. Clients that already hold a valid lease retain their IP
address (the lease lives in the client's kernel, not on the server) and their existing
TCP sessions remain intact — hence the asymmetry between "rebooted PC can't get an IP"
and "currently-up PCs are fine." The fault affects every internal VLAN simultaneously
because they all share the single server. Root cause: the dhcpd process on r1 exited
(crash or deliberate stop), leaving a stale PID file that prevents a clean restart.
Corrective fix: remove /var/run/dhcpd.pid on r1 then restart the service
("rm /var/run/dhcpd.pid && service isc-dhcp-server start"). Optionally configure
a process supervisor or systemd watchdog to auto-restart dhcpd on failure.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly identifies the affected device as r1 (multiple references: 'on r1', 'R1 hosts', 'r1's loopback').
The report explicitly identifies the isc-dhcp-server/dhcpd process on r1 as the failed component.
The agent explicitly explains that clients with existing valid leases retain their IPs and keep sessions, while new or rebooted clients cannot obtain addresses from the dead dhcpd.
Recommends removing the stale /var/run/dhcpd.pid and restarting the isc-dhcp-server on r1, which matches the expected remediation.

The investigation log contains explicit observations (r1 loopback 10.0.0.76, stale /var/run/dhcpd.pid with PID 87, kill -0 reports no such process, ps shows no dhcpd, dswa/dswb relays pointing to 10.0.0.76) that support the agent's conclusion that the ISC DHCP server on r1 is not running and is the cause of site-wide DHCP failures. The writeup's small assertion that the stale PID blocks a clean restart is plausible but wasn't directly exercised in the logs.
